purpose: Source register for skeleton-first canonical proportion work. Values are evidence inputs, not hard production targets.
policy: Use multiple independent sources; preserve population/method context; do not scale a single-study mean directly into the character without cross-checking.

sources.note: Already integrity-checked in proportion_report.json; direct bony forearm regression still to be computed reproducibly from the committed CSV.

sources.citation: Beredjiklian PK et al. Correlation between Adult Height and Metacarpal Length Using Advanced Imaging Modalities. Arch Bone Jt Surg. 2025;13(6):345-348.
sources.population: 40 skeletally mature adults; 28 men, 12 women; mean height 175.3 cm
use: cross-check hand ray ordering and scale
sources.limitation: Mixed-sex small sample; thumb value not in accessible abstract; do not stature-scale as a sole target.

sources.citation: Mathematical relations between the lengths of the metacarpal bones and phalanges: surgical significance.
sources.limitation: Single regional sample and 2D radiographs; use with the independent 2025 CT means and the character's stature-conditioned ANSUR hand-length corridor before freezing targets.
sources.measurement_definition: Head and base limits of each metacarpal/phalanx; midpoint-to-midpoint proximodistal length on standardized AP hand radiographs.

reported_relations.metacarpals: M1 = 0.67*M2 = 0.71*M3 = 0.78*M4 = 0.84*M5 (paper notation expresses equivalent pairwise ratios; Table 1 should be used for exact pairwise conversion).
reported_relations.note: Use the descriptive male means/SDs above for the first canonical corridor; pairwise ratios are a secondary shape check.

sources.citation: Hoang D et al. An Anatomical Study of Metacarpal Morphology Utilizing CT Scans. J Hand Surg Am. 2021.
sources.limitation: Accessible abstract does not expose numerical per-ray lengths.

sources.citation: Evaluation of metatarsal relationships in the biomechanics of 332 normal feet using the method of measuring relative lengths.
sources.normal_pattern: Index-minus most frequent; all three metatarsal formulas can be normal.
sources.limitation: Radiographic relative-length method is not identical to osteometric bone length; use ratios/patterns before absolute values.

sources.citation: Dogan A et al. Morphometric study of the human metatarsals and phalanges. Clin Anat. 2007;20(2):209-214.
use: metatarsal and toe phalanx internal proportions
sources.limitation: Accessible abstract confirms fixed proportions but does not expose the numerical formulas; full table/formulas required before final target.

sources.citation: Morphological and morphometric analysis of tarsal bones according to sex. Surg Radiol Anat. 2024.
sources.sample: 630 tarsal bones reconstructed from thin-section CT
sources.limitation: Accessible abstract exposes area/volume ordering, not linear bone lengths.

sources.citation: Measurement of three-dimensional morphological characteristics of the calcaneus using CT image post-processing.
use: calcaneus length/height geometry and sex/height adjustment
sources.limitation: Accessible abstract confirms measured parameters and height-adjusted sex analysis but not numerical values.

sources.citation: Hind- and midfoot bone morphology varies with foot type and sex.
use: shape variability bounds for calcaneus, talus, navicular, cuboid
sources.limitation: Useful for variability/shape classes, not a single canonical length.
Model-specific generic geometries; never used as the sole anatomical truth.

sources.citation: Ozaslan A et al. Estimation of stature and determination of sex from radial and ulnar bone lengths in a Turkish corpse sample. Forensic Sci Int. 2006.
sources.population: 80 male and 47 female recent forensic cases; mean ages 36 and 30 years
sources.limitation: Accessible abstract confirms regressions but does not expose coefficients or means; full table required before setting a numeric canonical target.

sources.citation: Torimitsu S et al. Stature estimation based on radial and ulnar lengths using three-dimensional images from multidetector computed tomography in a Japanese population. Leg Med. 2014.
sources.limitation: Population-specific; accessible abstract gives SEE but not coefficients/mean lengths.

sources.citation: Gul H et al. Estimation of Body Stature Using the Percutaneous Length of Ulna of an Individual. Cureus. 2020.
sources.limitation: Percutaneous ulna definition is not dry-bone maximum length and population-specific; use only as a cross-check, never as the primary skeletal target.

sources.citation: Meadows L, Jantz RL. Allometric secular change in the long bones from the 1800s to the present. J Forensic Sci. 1995.
use: guard against constant-ratio scaling of long bones
sources.finding: Upper-limb long bones were approximately isometric with stature; lower-limb bones showed positive allometry and secular change.
sources.limitation: Historical US male samples; informs scaling policy, not a target length.

sources.citation: Malone PSC et al. Anatomic Relationships of the Distal and Proximal Radioulnar Joints Articulating Surface Areas and of the Radius and Ulna Bone Volumes. Front Bioeng Biotechnol. 2016.
sources.population: 24 cadaver forearms for joint surfaces; 44 matched radius/ulna pairs for bone volume
use: forearm paired-bone relationship and PRUJ/DRUJ anatomy
sources.limitation: Volume and articular area relationships are not length ratios.

sources.citation: Barrôco R et al. Evaluation of metatarsal relationships in the biomechanics of 332 normal feet using the method of measuring relative lengths. Rev Bras Ortop. 2011/2015.
sources.population: 166 adults aged 25-50; 83 men and 83 women; 332 normal weight-bearing feet
sources.normal_pattern: Index-minus most frequent; M1 about 2.4 mm shorter than M2, M3 4.4 mm shorter than M2, M4 9.2 mm shorter than M3, M5 14.7 mm shorter than M4.
use: forefoot ray ordering and relative pattern under weight bearing
sources.limitation: Measurements are relative distances from a Chopart reference line to metatarsal heads, not osteometric metatarsal bone lengths.

sources.citation: Kwon BK et al. Morphologic evaluation of cervical spine anatomy with computed tomography: anterior cervical plate fixation considerations. J Spinal Disord Tech. 2004.
sources.population: CT studies from 50 males and 50 females
sources.limitation: Primarily body width/depth, not inter-level centre positions or disc-centre spacing.

sources.citation: Disc and Vertebral Body Morphology From Birth to Adulthood. Spine. 2022.
use: adult vertebral body/disc height plausibility and regional trend
sources.limitation: Growth-study endpoint values are regional summaries, not per-level adult male canonical coordinates.

sources.citation: Cross-sectional properties of rib geometry from an adult population. Front Bioeng Biotechnol. 2023.
use: population-derived rib cross-sectional geometry by rib number and normalized rib position
sources.limitation: Cross-section geometry does not by itself provide the full curved rib centreline or costovertebral axis.

sources.citation: Patil S et al. Radiological Biometric Study of Metatarsals and Phalanges. J Clin Diagn Res. 2017;11(9):AC05-AC09.
sources.population: 60 healthy adults >21 years; 33 men and 27 women; male mean age 27.78 years
sources.measurement_definition: Metatarsal length: most distal head point to midpoint of base articular surface; fifth metatarsal excludes styloid process. Phalanges: midpoint of proximal articular surface to midpoint of distal articular surface on standardized AP radiographs.
use: confirm whether a003 long foot is skeletal as well as surface
sources.limitation: Single regional sample and 2D radiographs. Distal phalanx comparison to a003 is weaker because the current armature distal tip can include a surface-tip allowance.

sources.citation: Patterson RM et al. Carpal bone anatomy measured by computer analysis of three-dimensional reconstructions of computed tomography images. J Hand Surg Am. 1995.
use: reject equal-length schematic carpal row as freeze-ready geometry
sources.limitation: Accessible abstract gives ordering but not all numerical maximum lengths.

sources.citation: Canovas F et al. Study of carpal bone morphology and position in three dimensions by image analysis from computed tomography scans of the wrist. Surg Radiol Anat. 2004.
use: relative 3D spacing independent of surface mesh
sources.limitation: Small sample; only selected normalized distances exposed in abstract.

sources.citation: Three-dimensional carpal alignment: computer-aided CT analysis of carpal axes and normal ranges. J Hand Surg Eur Vol. 2023.
sources.limitation: Angles depend on the study's radial coordinate system; must map frames explicitly before applying.

sources.citation: Postero-anterior radiography of the wrist. Normal database of carpal measurements. Surg Radiol Anat. 1998.
sources.limitation: 2D radiographic lengths and horn dimensions are not directly identical to 3D maximum-length or centroid-axis definitions.

sources.citation: Mahakkanukrauh P et al. Sex estimation from upper limb bones in a Thai population. Anat Cell Biol. 2020;53(1):36-43.

measurement_definitions.max_humerus: Most superior point on humeral head to most inferior point on trochlea.
measurement_definitions.max_ulna: Most superior point on olecranon to most inferior point on styloid.
measurement_definitions.physiological_ulna: Most distal point on coronoid-process surface to most distal point on inferior surface of distal ulnar head.
measurement_definitions.max_radius: Most proximally positioned point on radial head to styloid tip, without regard for long axis.

use: maximum ulna/humerus plausibility after endpoint conversion
sources.limitation: Population-specific direct osteometry. Current a003 ulna maximum requires an estimated olecranon allowance, so radius is the cleaner comparison.

sources.citation: Forensic Anthropology reference text/table: male Aboriginal left radius and ulna dimensions.
sources.limitation: Reference-table source rather than the primary measurement publication; left side only. Use as corroboration, not the sole target.

sources.citation: Pretorius HS, Ferreira N, Burger MC. A computer tomography-based anthropomorphic study of forearm osteology: implications for prosthetic design. SA Orthop J. 2021;20(3).
sources.population: 97 adult forearm CT scans; 84% male; mean age 34.91 years

measurement_definition.radius: overall length from midpoint of wrist to centre of radial head
measurement_definition.ulna: overall length from midpoint of olecranon to centre of distal ulna

use: measurement-defined adult CT cross-check for radius/ulna segment geometry
distal radius soft/landmark conversion sanity check
sources.limitation: Predominantly male but not male-only; mean stature not reported; radius endpoint is wrist midpoint rather than radial styloid and ulna endpoint is olecranon midpoint rather than maximum olecranon tip.

sources.citation: Rausch V et al. The radial head size in relation to osseous landmarks of the forearm. Surg Radiol Anat. 2019.
use: secondary forearm length and radial-head scale cross-check
sources.limitation: Mixed-sex cadaver sample; accessible abstract does not fully expose endpoint definitions, so it cannot freeze canonical length.

sources.citation: Gender Variation in the Shape of Superior Talar Dome: A Cadaver Measurement Based on Chinese Population. 2018.
sources.limitation: Cadaveric Chinese sample; talus length definition is study-specific and not the same as the current HGPT talus control-stick span.

sources.citation: Morphometric Analysis of the Calcaneus in a Southeast Asian Population. 2024.
sources.limitation: Regional population; axial maximum length is not directly comparable with the current HGPT calcaneus reference-stick span.

sources.citation: Anthropometric Analysis of Cuboid Bones in a South Indian Population. 2023.
sources.limitation: Sex unknown and dry-bone sample; not a direct joint-centre distance.

sources.citation: Intrinsic proportions of the human tarsus: an original approach to tarsal biometry. Surg Radiol Anat. 2003.
use: tarsal hierarchy and posterior/anterior mass balance
sources.limitation: Mass proportions, not linear dimensions.

sources.citation: Celik NG, Akman B. Morphological and morphometric analysis of tarsal bones according to sex. Surg Radiol Anat. 2024.
sources.sample: 630 tarsal bones reconstructed from thin-section CT
sources.finding: All male area and volume values were significantly larger than female values.
sources.limitation: Accessible abstract exposes ordering but not linear dimensions.

sources.citation: Holcombe SA, Wang SC, Grotberg JB. The effect of age and demographics on rib shape. J Anat. 2017.
sources.population: 1042 live adults; 535 male and 507 female CT scans; ages 20-99
sources.coverage: 20,627 ribs; centroidal path geometry with six-parameter shape and three-parameter orientation models
findings: height and sex strongly associated with rib size
weight strongly associated with pump-handle angle
age affects rib aspect ratio/end-to-end separation more than arc length
sources.limitation: Requires the paper/model parameter mapping to reconstruct exact rib-level curves; not reducible to one universal rib length.

sources.citation: Characterization of the centroidal geometry of human ribs. J Biomech. 2013.
sources.population: 16 adult male cadavers; rib levels 2-10; 144 CT-extracted ribs
findings: upper ribs 2-5 are closer to circular
posterior curvature is less pronounced in lower ribs
use: rib-level curvature topology and curved-centreline validation
sources.limitation: Male cadaver sample is small; rib 1, 11 and 12 are not covered.

sources.citation: A parametric ribcage geometry model accounting for variations among the adult population. J Biomech. 2016.
sources.geometry: 12 rib pairs + sternum + thoracic spine, 1016 landmarks/subject, symmetry adjusted
sources.limitation: Exact coefficients/landmarks must be transcribed before a numeric canonical chest can be generated.

sources.citation: A statistical human rib cage geometry model accounting for variations by age, sex, stature and body mass index. J Biomech. 2014.
sources.population: 89 adult CT scans approximately balanced by age and sex
sources.limitation: Model coefficients required before direct reconstruction.

sources.citation: Morphometric analysis of variation in the ribs with age and sex. J Anat. 2014.
use: age/sex variation and rib-level orientation cross-check
sources.limitation: Focuses on statistical shape variation rather than simple bone lengths.

sources.citation: Cross-sectional properties of rib geometry from an adult population. Front Bioeng Biotechnol. 2023.
use: rib envelope/cortical geometry after centreline reconstruction
sources.limitation: Cross-section geometry alone does not define centreline or joint axis.

sources.citation: Age-related changes in osseous anatomy, alignment, and range of motion of the cervical spine. Part I. Eur Spine J. 2012.
sources.population: 1,230 asymptomatic volunteers; >=100 men and >=100 women per decade from 20s to 70s
sources.limitation: Radiographic mid-body/disc heights; C1/C2 require separate anatomy.

sources.citation: Morphometric analysis of the relationships between intervertebral disc and vertebral body heights: anatomical and radiographic study of the human thoracic spine. 2011.
sources.limitation: Sample/method differs from CT studies and values are generally smaller than some population CT datasets; use as one corridor bound, not sole target.

sources.citation: Computed tomographic-based morphometric study of thoracic spine and its relevance to anaesthetic and spinal surgical procedures. 2016.
use: level trend and kyphotic anterior/posterior difference
sources.limitation: Population-specific CT sample; sex-combined values in the accessible table.

sources.citation: Morphological characteristics of lumbar vertebral bodies and regional distribution patterns of bone mineral density: a CT study. 2026.
sources.limitation: Sex-combined level table; body-height geometry only, not disc height.

sources.citation: Morphometric Analysis of Lumbar Intervertebral Disc Height: An Imaging Study. World Neurosurg. 2019.
sources.population: 240 healthy abdominal CT scans; 109 men and 131 women
sources.limitation: Average of anterior/centre/posterior disc heights; age span broad.

sources.citation: Morphometric Analysis of Clavicle and Its Medullary Canal: A Computed Tomographic Study. 2020.
sources.limitation: Regional CT sample; true clavicle centreline/curved length, not straight SC-to-AC chord.

sources.citation: The anatomy of the clavicle: a three-dimensional cadaveric study. Clin Anat. 2014.

male_values_mm.endpoint_length_note: overall sample endpoint length 149.4 ± 10.3 mm; male-specific endpoint mean not exposed in abstract

sources.limitation: Cadaver sample older; endpoint and centreline definitions must not be mixed.

sources.citation: Osseous anatomy of the scapula. Clin Orthop Relat Res. 2001.
sources.limitation: Small cadaver sample; mixed sex.

sources.citation: Predetermining glenoid dimensions using the scapular dimensions. 2018.
sources.limitation: Dry/cadaveric morphology; population-specific.

sources.citation: Determination of Sexual Dimorphism of the Human Sacrum Based on ROC Curve Analysis of Morphometric Parameters. 2023.
sources.limitation: Regional dry-bone sample; does not define SI joint centre or pelvic orientation.

sources.citation: Sacrum morphometry and spinopelvic parameters among the Indonesian population using computed tomography scans. 2021.
sources.population: 300 adults; 150 men and 150 women; median age 35
sources.finding: Curved and straight sacral lengths were greater in males; ventral breadth greater in females.
sources.limitation: Accessible excerpt does not expose all sex-specific means.

sources.citation: Morphometric Examination of the Sacroiliac Region and Variable Positions of the Sacral Auricular Surface. 2023.
use: SI region variability and sacral dimension corridor
sources.limitation: Auricular-surface groups vary; not a single canonical SI centre.

sources.citation: Human coxal bone sexual dimorphism and multislice computed tomography: geometric morphometric analysis of 65 adults. J Forensic Sci. 2012.
sources.population: 65 Caucasian adults; 15 osteometric landmarks on 3D reconstructed coxae
use: os coxae landmark topology and male-shape corridor
sources.limitation: Accessible abstract does not expose the numerical landmark coordinates/distances.

sources.citation: Shape variability of the adult human acetabulum and acetabular fossa related to sex and age by geometric morphometrics. Forensic Sci Int. 2017.
sources.sample: 682 os coxae from three documented skeletal collections
use: acetabular rim/fossa shape variability and sex-aware morphology
sources.limitation: Shape model rather than a simple joint-centre target; HJC remains governed by separate regression/landmark evidence.

sources.citation: MRI analysis of the physiological patellofemoral joint morphology of adult knees. Skeletal Radiol. 2025.
sources.limitation: MRI soft-tissue/cartilage context differs from dry-bone dimensions; width male-specific value not exposed in snippet.

sources.citation: Sex Estimation Using Patellar Morphometry: Evidence from a Late Roman Population in Anatolia. 2025.
sources.limitation: Archaeological population; use as secondary morphology check.

sources.citation: Anatomical examination of the fibula: digital imaging study for osseointegrated implant installation. 2015.
sources.measurement_definition: apex of fibular head to apex of lateral malleolus
sources.limitation: Small regional sample.

sources.citation: Sexual Dimorphism of the Nutrient Foramen of the Fibula and Its Importance in Vascularised Bone Grafting. 2023.
sources.limitation: Regional dry-bone sample; exact endpoint wording should be preserved from full paper if used for final freeze.

sources.citation: Non-linear scaling of a musculoskeletal model of the lower limb using statistical shape models. 2019.
use: whole lower-limb proportion cross-check at similar statures
sources.limitation: Small illustrative subject set, not a population target; segment definitions are model-specific.

unresolved_source_needs: Direct adult male radius and ulna numerical length distributions or regression coefficients with explicit osteometric/CT landmark definitions from an accessible full source.
Numerical metacarpal-to-phalange formulas from a full accessible hand morphometry source.
Numerical metatarsal-to-phalange formulas and tarsal linear dimensions from full accessible foot morphometry sources.
Curved rib centreline/axis orientation by rib level, not only cross-sectional geometry.
Per-level vertebral body/disc centre spacing and sagittal alignment across C2-S1 with consistent adult-male definitions.
